reason: Prior measurements show no repeatable gain for the tested classical variants, so I rank the approved, unmeasured Strassen path first: it reduces the subproduct MAC count, though timed packing, recombination, and FP32 error are major risks. The two Strassen workspace proposals are close behind; they share the same algorithm, and their effects should not be credited separately if tested jointly. A smaller A panel and fused transpose have plausible data-movement benefits but substantial unverified costs. The ZA mapping permutation has little evidence for a speedup. Tail handling and the C fallback affect general sizes rather than the fixed n=512 timing path. The n512_fast_path proposal duplicates the main Strassen recommendation. I rank assembly_audit last because the supplied evidence says the proposed SME2 post-index load form is unverified and a related direct-gather proposal failed compilation; do not treat either as a performance result.
